dee72010f5.q: How has the M&A deal closure timeline changed from the 1990s to today, and what factors have extended the sales process?
dee72010f5.a: In the 1990s, deals could close in 5-6 months; today they typically take 8-9 months or longer. Virtual data rooms, which have only proliferated in the last 20 years, allow buyers to analyze extensive information and trend lines, creating longer review processes. Additional delays come from quality of earnings reports (4-8 weeks), buyer due diligence, and representations and warranty insurance. While these tools provide better risk mitigation and more thorough analysis, they collectively extend the deal cycle considerably compared to the era when companies met in conference rooms with physical boxes of documents.

e8d3761145.q: What is the financial model of an investment bank, and why is it challenging to forecast and manage?
